title: Minnesota lawyer suspended over fake AI case citations

reading.body:
An attorney submitted a legal memorandum to a Minnesota court containing two citations to cases that do not exist. The citations were generated by an AI system and presented as factual legal authority. The opposing attorney discovered the fabrication before the judge ruled on the case.

This is a failure in the deployment of AI as a legal research tool. The system generated false citations with confidence, and the attorney used them without verification. No human check on the AI output occurred before filing. It would have taken a review step, such as spot-checking citations against legal databases, to catch the false cases before submission.

Whether the attorney intended to deceive the court or relied uncritically on the AI system is not established by the reporting.

reports.title: Minnesota lawyer suspended over fake AI case citations

summary:
A Minnesota attorney named Faisal S. Ahmed was suspended for submitting fake legal citations generated by artificial intelligence in a court filing. Ahmed cited two nonexistent cases, Anderson v. City of Biwabik and Doherty v. Alma E. Clark Memorial Home, in a 2025 legal memorandum filed in Hennepl County Court to support his client's position in a civil dispute over unpaid rent. The opposing attorney discovered the fabricated cases and informed the judge of the likely AI hallucinations.

Judge Lois Conroy ruled against Ahmed's client and ordered payment of $233,563 in back rent. She fined Ahmed $5,000 and referred him to the state's Professional Responsibility Board. According to the Office of Lawyers Professional Responsibility, Ahmed agreed to a 30-day suspension of his law license and must pay an additional $900 in costs. The judge noted that over 800 documented instances of fake AI citations have been catalogued, emphasizing that attorneys must maintain ethical obligations regardless of using artificial intelligence tools.
